target.title: feat: prefer token-free transports before metered API quota
target.body:
Anonymous API quota and pooled identities are both metered and contended; public HTML pages, raw.githubusercontent, and git smart HTTP are effectively unmetered. The worker previously preferred the anonymous API candidate and only tried token-free transports first once anonymous quota dropped below 50%.

This flips the ordering: whenever a route offers both, validated token-free transports run FIRST, with anonymous API and then pooled identities as the same-cycle fallback chain. A token-free parser miss still falls through to the API candidate in the same request, so correctness is unchanged — the fallback chain is the safety mechanism, no config flag needed.

- The single central gate in `callGitHubWeb` becomes unconditional; the below-half threshold read and the deferred-API-payload machinery are dead and deleted (including the stored-rate query in sql/queries + generated code). API rate snapshots are still recorded for observability.
- Exact-REST-semantics requests (custom media types via the single-candidate path, conditional headers) are untouched; only multi-candidate ordering changes.
- Shape validation and public-visibility proofs unchanged.
- Docs updated across cache.md / token-free.md / relay.md / operations.md / README.

Proof: 185 vitest tests green (fetch-order, parser-miss fallback, media-path, rate-independence coverage), `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint/format clean. Autoreview (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): clean first pass, "patch is correct".

Requires a wrangler deploy to take effect; `octopool stats` route mixes will show the before/after (pooled backend share should drop on run/pr/release summary and contents routes).
